items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: Now, of course, I ain't put them like Howard and Clayton and all that.

ctx.x: Albert Warner is your, uh... That's my first cousin.

Your first cousin. Yeah. Well, he ain't been playing as long as me. No. Yeah, he come out with a horn. The bell must have been about that big. Old horn he had. And he started learning. And I believe Shalini learned him. I'd play a trampoline. So that's make, I says, well, I says, now, I said, Warnick, I say, Pajou's dead now, eh? I say, he said, yeah, I don't know who they got. I said, well, the best man would fit that would be, Charlie Love or Peter Bocard. Of course, I said, I don't say that they got a rag.…
That's right. You can say you're doing the best you can. What was that place you were telling us about, a second of the magazine when Freddie and...

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1957-08-04
items.q: that's a little Kid Howard, but I don't know, I've been in a little, little 2x4 band, like myself, when I first started, and he was playing drum, and now he's playing carnet, and he's playing pretty bad carnet too, I must say that about him, and he's a nice fella

ctx.x: well, sure, I mean, if you don't keep doing it all,

yes, and, nevertheless, I don't take him, I just, it takes interest into it, no more, you see, because I'm getting old, or young something, some people call them old man, some call them young man, so I don't know what I am, you know, so, I just say, well, so I made different things, I made records with this fellow, they called Joe Nicholas, and, when Joe, they called him for nickname, but I called him, Joe Nicklaus, well, they know him from Joe Nicklaus, but I called him Wooden Joe sometimes too, so we played at…
but who plays it though, Mr. Sire,
